post.caption: Chocolate diamonds were once just brown. Brown diamonds were long treated as low value stones. Many went to industry, where they drilled rock and cut glass. In Australia, almost 80 percent of Argyle's diamonds were brown. Argyle graded its browns from lightest to darkest, C1 to C7. In the 1980s, advertisers swapped brown for names like champagne and cognac. In 2000, Le Vian branded some of them Chocolate Diamonds. Eddie LeVian picked the word after a friend brought handmade chocolates. Le Vian trademarked the name, so rivals used words like coffee. Argyle stopped mining on November 3, 2020, after 37 years.
